postings.title: Analyst
postings.description:
At SHAPE, the strategic command that plans and directs NATO operations, you will be the analytical voice that helps SACEUR and the Command Group see crises coming before they unfold. As a Political and Security Analyst within the Operations Directorate, you will assess adversary and competitor dynamics, with a particular focus on Russia, deterrence, and escalation, and turn complex political and security developments into clear, compelling briefings that directly inform operational planning and strategic decision-making. If you have a strong track record in political and security analysis, a deep understanding of Russia's strategic behaviour, the ability to explain complex issues simply, and the curiosity to apply new analytical tools (including AI) to hard problems, this is a rare opportunity to see your analysis shape real-world Alliance decisions.

1. Post Context:

The Strategic Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) is NATO’s strategic command responsible for planning and directing NATO operations, missions, and activities to support the Alliance’s objectives.

The Operations Directorate monitors the strategic environment and manages current operations for Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR), providing operational and policy advice.

The Political and Security Analysis Branch (PSA) supports this work by analysing political and security developments to help the SHAPE Command Group understand emerging and ongoing crises, especially where they affect NATO interests.

The Analyst focuses on adversary and competitor dynamics in the context of the Alliance and SACEUR’s responsibilities.

2. Principal Duties:

1. Within an assigned geographic or thematic area, leads analyses and forecasts political and security developments that impact SHAPE’s crisis identification, operational planning, assessment, and strategic awareness.
2. Prepares clear and compelling reports, point papers, and briefings about how political and security developments affect the Alliance, its military instrument of power, and operational planning.
3. Cultivates and maintains an external network of experts from universities, think tanks, research organisations, international organisations, and national governments.
4. Maintains routine communication and timely exchange of information with counterparts throughout ACO, NATO Headquarters, and other NATO entities.

3. Special Requirements and Additional Duties

The employee may be required to perform a similar range of duties elsewhere within the organisation at the same grade without there being any change to the contract.

The incumbent may be required to undertake deployments in support of military operations and exercises, and/or TDY assignments, both within and without NATO boundaries. Such operational deployment may exceed 30 days duration up to 183 days in any period of 547 days, and may be on short notice. For NATO International Civilian Staff, acceptance of an employment contract linked to this post constitutes agreement to deploy in excess of 30 days if required.

4. Essential Qualifications

a. Professional Experience
1. Recent experience in a government, non-government, international, or private sector organisations with a responsibility related to political and security analysis.
2. Experienced in regions of relevance to the Alliance ideally with expertise in relevant areas of conflict analysis, primarily political, economic and social dimensions.

b. Education and Training
1. University Degree in a related discipline and 2 years of post-related experience, or Higher Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training in that discipline leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 4 years post-related experience.
2. In case of ambiguity the required post-specific experience has priority over the standard education and training levels and experience described here.

c. Language
1. English - SLP 3333 - (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

5. Desirable Qualifications

a. Professional Experience

1. Substantial experience with analysis of political and security dynamics related to Russia, deterrence, and escalation dynamics.
2. Experience in NATO strategy, consultation, planning, and operations.
3. Lead authorship of at least 3 publications (related to political and security analysis) in external peer-reviewed journals or equivalent government venues.
4. Experience applying artificial intelligence tools and methods to complex analytical problems, including integrating AI into analytical workflows and critically evaluating outputs for accuracy, bias, and relevance.

b. Language
1. English - SLP 4444 - (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

6. Attributes and Competencies

• Personal Attributes: Motivated, flexible, highly collaborative team player and effective communicator. Able to convey complex problems simply; open to new analytical and problem-solving techniques.

• Professional Contacts: Collaborates as required with subject matter experts and customers across SHAPE staff, ACO-subordinate commands and other information partners (i.e. international, governmental and non-governmental organizations, centres of excellence, and academia) to obtain necessary information/analysis to support ACO's knowledge requirements.

• Contribution To Objectives: Lead of analytical work on specific elements of the Operations Directorate’s processes, the incumbent is the academic integrator of experts from other contributing disciplines and organizations cooperating in the analysis area. He/she delivers the contents of the comprehensive and dynamic situation awareness to commanders and planners by means of briefings, planning sessions, or short deployments to the operations area

REMARKS:
• Duration of contract: Serving staff members will be offered a contract according to the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations (NCPR). Newly recruited staff will be offered a definite duration contract of three years normally followed by an indefinite duration contract.
• The salary will be the basic entry-level monthly salary defined by the NATO Grade of the post, which may be augmented by allowances based on the selected staff member’s eligibility, and which is subject to the withholding of approximately 20% for pension and medical insurance contributions.
• NATO is committed to diversity and inclusion, and strives to provide equal access to employment, advancement, and retention, independent of gender, age, nationality, ethnic origin, religion or belief, cultural background, sexual orientation, and disability. NATO welcomes applications of nationals from all member Nations.
• Building integrity is a key element of NATO’s core tasks. As an employer, NATO values commitment to the principles of integrity, transparency, and accountability in accordance with international norms and practices established for the defence and related security sector. Selected candidates are expected to be role models of integrity, and to promote good governance through ongoing efforts in their work.
• Applicants who prove to be competent for the post but who are not successful in this competition may be offered an appointment in another post of a similar nature, which might become vacant in the near future, albeit at the same or lower grade, provided they meet the necessary requirements.

• We believe that all people are capable of great things. Because of this, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet all of the criteria listed within this job description.
• Shortlisted candidates will be requested to provide original documentary evidence and a set of copies supporting statements in their applications. Appointment is subject to obtaining a NS security clearance and a medical certificate.
• Only nationals from the 32 NATO member states can apply for vacancies at SHAPE.
• Applications are automatically acknowledged within one working day after submission. In the absence of an acknowledgement please make sure the submission process is completed, or, re-submit the application.
• Qualified redundant staff of the same grade interested in this post should inform this office, via their HR/Personnel Office by not later than vacancy’s closing date.
• NATO will not accept any phase of the recruitment and selection prepared, in whole or in part, by means of generative artificial-intelligence (AI) tools, including and without limitation to chatbots, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (Chat GPT), or other language generating tools. NATO reserves the right to screen applications to identify the use of such tools. All applications prepared, in whole or in part, by means of such generative or creative AI applications may be rejected without further consideration at NATO’s sole discretion, and NATO reserves the right to take further steps in such cases as appropriate.
• As part of the recruitment process, the organization may review publicly available information to assess potential conflicts of interest, reputational risks, or behaviors inconsistent with the organization’s values.

postings.title: Assistant (Purchasing and Contracting)
postings.description:
In a world full of uncertainties, NATO acts as a main pillar to maintain peace and stability. You are an experienced financial expert specialized in purchasing and contracting, why not joining our team? We offer not only a job with significant material benefits, but a meaningful mission.

1. POST CONTEXT AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The NATO Science & Technology Organization (STO) is a NATO subsidiary body to the North Atlantic Council (NAC), and is governed by the NATO Science and Technology Board (STB). The STB reports to the NAC through the Military Committee (MC) and the Conference of National Armaments Directors (CNAD).

The mission of the STO is to help position the Nations and NATO Bodies’ S&T investments as a strategic enabler of the knowledge and technical advantage supporting the defence and security posture of Allies and partner Nations. As described in the STO Charter, the STO Collaboration Support Office (CSO) is one of the three Executive Bodies of the STO.

Within the framework of the STO Collaborative business model, the CSO provides executive and administrative support to the S&T activities conducted through the eight STO Scientific and Technical Committees (STCs). The CSO facilitates the world’s largest and most vibrant scientific network for defence and security. More than 5 000 scientists and engineers from NATO and Partner Nations are engaged in approximately 460 carefully selected S&T Activities in the Collaborative Programme of Work (CPoW). Together, they work to solve real-world problems that Nations face today, and to better prepare their Armed Forces to meet future challenges. In its areas of expertise, the CSO provides assistance and support to the NATO Science and Technology Board (STB), its Chair, the Chief Scientist, and his/her office.

The CSO Budget & Finance Branch is responsible for all budgetary, fiscal, procurement and disbursing activities of the CSO within authorized and delegated budgets. The Science & Technology Organization (STO) Collaboration Support Office (CSO) is looking for an assistant who will be responsible for General Purchasing and Contracting. The incumbent shall be capable to operate the entire procurement workflow with limited supervision.

Functions include:

CSO is currently and for the coming years facing a very exciting yet challenging period with the implementation of a new ambition decided by NATO Nations and reflected in a 2030 vision and strategy.

The incumbent will be embedded in a very dynamic multi-national team of financial and operational experts.

He/she is responsible for General Purchasing and Contracting; in particular:

· Reviewing and processing commitments requests from fund managers, assessing their propriety within the budget and fiscal rules which cover the whole range of procurements, service and staff costs;

· Assisting the Staff Officer in the control he/she exercises on P&C requisitions to verify the compliance with NFRs and the STO Financial Procedures;

· Reviewing, editing, and recommending wording of technical specifications to be used in solicitations to ensure it is understandable from a commercial perspective;

· Screening firms as potential bidders, creating inputs and maintaining supplier data in the Supplier Management Database. Staying abreast, on own initiative, of new market trends, e-commerce and technology developments;

· Supporting customer requests for deviation, if in the best interest of the CSO, from normal method of procurement by participating in basic market research;

· For simplified procurement soliciting offers in accordance with established thresholds;

· Suggesting and drafting bidding instructions and contract clauses to be applied to all solicitations including Invitation for International bids;

· Supporting the conduct of international and formal competitive bidding procedures;

· Assisting the Contracting Officer in organizing bidders’ conferences, site surveys, inspections, progress review meetings, and other contractual events;

· Supporting the evaluations of bids and contract award recommendations;

· Investigating the financial viability of vendors/contractors before contracts are awarded when considered necessary;

· Providing administrative support to the Contracting Officer’s input to the Contract Award Committee;

· Assisting of the Staff Officer (Fiscal, Accounting / P&C Officer) in disputes resolution and proposals for settlement;

· Administering the contract files including into archive and eventual destruction;

· Participating in the education of customers and bidders to promote good procurement practices, best standard of conduct and efficient contracting tools and methods.

· Receiving and examining all invoices concerning the delivery, prices, calculation, discounts and contract; clarify discrepancies with respective CSO Requestor / Fund Managers upon their inspection of goods received and services rendered, tracks them in the database.

· Liaise with CSO PAL Branch when procurement related matters bear issues relevant to privileges and immunities granted by the Host Nation.

The incumbent is expected to be eager and flexible to adapt and learn as the CSO and the Finance team go through the challenges of digital and organizational transformation. He/she is not afraid of embracing data-driven technology, digital innovation and AI-powered financial tools for predictive analytics and process automation to enhance efficiency and enable financial insights. He/she is motivated and willing to go beyond the expected and to be challenged by the unknown as the CSO Finance Team explores and defines new ways of working and pro-actively contributes to the achievements of these goals.

2. REPORTING LINES

This position reports to the Staff Officer (Fiscal, Accounting / P&C Officer). The post holder will be required to execute functions of other Assistants in BudFin as directed by the Branch Head in their absence.

3. QUALIFICATIONS

ESSENTIAL

The incumbent must demonstrate:

Professional /Experience

· At least 5 years professional experience in a business or finance related field, with extensive experience of at least 2 years in purchase and contracting procedures.

· Good knowledge of procurement regulations and extensive experience in administrative procurement procedures.

· Ability to conduct purchase and price negotiations.

· Demonstrated ability to work independently.

Education/Training

· Higher Secondary education and intermediate vocational training in supply chain management, commercial and mercantile law, logistics, inventory management, procurement or related discipline which might lead to a formal qualification with 3 years’ experience, or Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training in that discipline leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 4 years post related experience.

· Training in accounting & contracting practices and procedures, and in the use of Oracle/SAP Financial software or equivalent.

Language

Very good knowledge of French (SLP 3333), good working knowledge of the English (SLP 3232). Most of the work is conducted in French.

DESIRABLE

The following would be considered an advantage:

Professional /Experience

· Previous purchasing & contracting experience in international settings.

· Experienced user of financial software applications, in particular NATO FinS.

· An established relationship with agencies and NATO bodies involved in procurement.

· Previous experience in an Assistant position in an international environment, preferably in Finance & Contracting.

· Accounting knowledge and experience.

Education/Training

· Higher diploma from an accredited establishment in accounting and/or contracting.

· NATO-ACO Contingency Contracting Course (FIN-FI-31823) provided by NATO - School Oberammergau (NSO)

· E-commerce tools

· Tact and to steadiness to discuss / negotiate with potential providers / suppliers.

Language

· Very good knowledge of both NATO official languages.

· Knowledge of other European language(s).

4. COMPETENCIES

4.1. Personal Attributes

· Good moral character.

· Trustworthy, loyal and with a high sense of responsibility.

· Good judgment in the initiation and maintenance of business relationships.

· Good adaptability to new tasks.

4.2. Managerial Responsibilities

Not applicable

4.3. Professional Contacts

· Works with other CSO staff members in an interactive manner to identify, clarify and fulfil their requirements.

· Has daily contact with contractors.

4.4. Contribution to the Objectives

The Assistant, Purchasing & Contracting contributes to the mission of the CSO by ensuring the efficiency and the reliability of the CSO purchasing and contracting operations, and the follow up of the procedures in line with NATO Finance and IPSAS principles.

5. SECURITY CLEARANCE LEVEL

The applicant must be eligible for a NATO Secret security clearance.

6. WORKING ENVIRONMENT

The CSO operates in an international, dynamic, multi-cultural environment. The functions require regular business travel. The CSO is a non-smoking workplace.

7. EMPLOYMENT TERMS AND CONDITIONS

The position is at grade G 10. The starting basic monthly salary is Euro 5.335 (salary value as per 2026, subject to future adjustments in accordance with NAC decisions), exempt from income tax. Specific allowances may apply, depending on personal circumstances of the incumbent.

The post holder will benefit from 30 days annual leave, life and medical insurance, a retirement pension plan, education allowance for dependent children and biennial home leave if eligible.

The selected candidate will be offered a definite duration contract of three years including a six months probationary period. Upon performance, a follow-up definite or indefinite contract shall be offered to the incumbent.

The CSO Director will appoint the selected candidate through the signature of his/her contract. This contract will be ruled by the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations.

The appointment is subject to the receipt by the CSO of a security clearance at NATO SECRET level (provided by the national Authorities of the incumbent) and to the delivery of a certificate of medical fitness by the CSO Medical Advisor.

8. APPLICATION PROCEDURE

Only nationals of the 32 NATO member countries can apply for this position.

Applications must be submitted as follows, as applicable:

· For NATO serving civilian Staff members only: please apply via the internal recruitment portal (for more information, please contact your local Civilian HR Manager).

· For all other applicants: https://nato.taleo.net/careersection/2/jobsearch.ftl?lang=en.

A Selection Committee will evaluate the applications. Applicants who pass an initial screening by the Selection Committee will be evaluated by an assessment centre and invited to attend an interview with the Selection Committee in Paris, France beginning Dec 2026.

Candidates will attach a resume, an application letter and educational qualifications certificates to their application.

NATO will not accept any phase of the recruitment and selection prepared, in whole or in part, by means of reference documents without proper quotes (plagiarism), or any tools available on internet, including but not limited to translation facilities, or generative artificial-intelligence (AI) tools. NATO reserves the right to screen applications to identify the use of such tools. All applications prepared, in whole or in part, by means of such tools will be rejected without further consideration, and NATO reserves the right to take further steps in such cases as appropriate

NATO as employer values diverse backgrounds and perspectives and is committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and talented workforce. NATO welcomes applications of nationals from all NATO Nations and strongly encourages women to apply. According to the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations, Staff members are appointed on the condition that they are over 21 and under 60 years of age at the time of taking up their appointment. However, appointment may be offered to candidates of 60 years of age or more provided that the expiry date of the contract is not later than the date at which the candidate attains the age of 65.

Buyer
postings.description:
Our Requirement:

Title: Buyer

NATO International Civilian Grade: 10

Duty location: Wesel, Germany

Closing date for applications: 11 October 2026

NATO is establishing (in 2027) a 4th NATO Signal Battalion, part of the NATO CIS Group, located in Denmark. The 4th NATO Signal Battalion also has a Buyer position, identical to this position. Candidates applying for the 1st NSB position will be asked if they also would be interested in the upcoming 4th NSB Buyer position.

Our organisation:

1st NATO Signal Battalion operates, maintains, and sustains Deployable Communication Information Systems (DCIS) to enable command and control (C2) in support of deployed NATO Headquarters and entities during Alliance operations, missions and exercises. The Command Group provides and sustains command and control capabilities, in terms of support, coordination, management, administrative service, and specialists' advice to communication and information systems (CIS), in order to meet the CIS units’ mission. The S8 section plans and executes the 1st NSB’s budget. The incumbent is responsible for the purchasing activities in support of 1st NSB and its subordinated entities as well as in support of Missions, Exercises and other operational level tasks, effecting and managing the acquisition and orders administration for the procurement of goods and services. S/he provides purchasing expertise and P&C advisory services to the NSB Commander and subordinate units, in accordance with NCISG P&C Office Head guidance.

The main duties of Buyer are to:

Exercise the functions associated with being a Buyer in support of the procurement process throughout the entire procurement workflow for goods, services and/or engineering works by but not limited to the following:

Ø Review, edit, and recommend wording of technical specifications to be used in solicitations to ensure it is understandable from a commercial perspective.

Ø Screen firms as potential bidders, create inputs and maintain supplier data in the Supplier Management Database. Stay abreast of new market trends, e-commerce and technology developments. Support customer requests for deviation, if in the best interest of the Headquarters, from normal method of procurement by participating in basic market research.

Ø For simplified procurement solicit offers in accordance with established thresholds.

Ø Suggest and draft bidding instructions and contract clauses to be applied to all solicitations including Invitation for International Bids.

Ø Support the conduct of international and formal competitive bidding procedures.

Ø Assist the Contracting Officer in organizing bidders’ conferences, site surveys, inspections, progress review meetings, and other contractual events.

Ø Support the evaluations of bids and contract award recommendations.

Ø Investigate the financial viability of vendors/contractors before contracts are awarded (e.g., Dun & Bradstreet evaluations) when considered necessary.

Ø Provide administrative support to the Contracting Officer’s input to the Contract Award Committee.

Ø Assist of the Contracting Officer in disputes resolution and proposals for settlements.

Ø Administer the contract files including into archive and eventual destruction; and

Ø Participate in the education of customers and bidders to promote good procurement practices, best standard of conduct and efficient contracting tools and methods.

Special requirements and Additional Duties:

The incumbent may be required to undertake deployments in support of military operations and exercises, and/or TDY assignments, both within and without NATO boundaries. Such operational deployment may exceed 30 days duration up to 183 days in any period of 547 days, and may be on short notice. For NATO International Civilian Staff, acceptance of an employment contract linked to this post constitutes agreement to deploy in excess of 30 days if required.

Ø The employee may be required to perform a similar range of duties elsewhere within the organisation at the same grade without there being any change to the contract

Ø Prepares invitation for bids and purchase orders on behalf of the NCISG as directed by the NCISG P&C Office Head.

Ø For requisitions assigned to him/her within limited warrant authority, is responsible for the complete procurement process (from cradle to grave).

Ø Formulates and executes acquisition strategy through source selection procedures in obtaining minimum competitive quotes in accordance with NATO Financial Regulations and procurement directives and policies. Drafts bidding instructions and routine contract clauses to be applied to solicitations and submits them to the approval of the Contracting Officer. As directed by the later coordinates related matters with the NCISG Legal Office, NCISG HQ Divisions, 1NSBs Branches, M&S Coys and DCMs Sections.

Ø Evaluates bids and executes award decisions within the limited warrant authority

Ø Creates standard purchase orders and supplementary paperwork for goods and services (including but not limited to Statement of Works, Statement of Requirements)

Ø Provides expertise and continuity for NCISG Purchase and Contracting activities and other projects as assigned and acquisition planning and management.

Ø Screens requests for deviation from standard procurement procedures and undertakes appropriate actions to get the necessary approvals to support the requirements.

Ø Responsible for control of standard purchase orders and both service and supply type contract purchase agreements.

Ø Serves in the function as assigned in the Purchase Card Programme.

Ø Promotes customer relations and good business practices by education end-user on efficient procurement methods, tools, procedures.

Ø Oversees comprehensive/systematic contract filling system and ensures proper archiving and destruction of contract documents/files.

Ø Provides assistance to database management and proposes (or processes when authorized) inclusions, exclusions, deletions, etc. of vendor data included in the Supplier Database.

Ø Operates an Automated Accounting/Purchasing Application System for the execution and follow up of requisitions, purchase orders, invoices, receipts, reports.

Ø Assists the Contracting Officers in settling possible disputes/claims with contractors in a manner consistent with contractual obligations.

Ø Liaises and coordinates procurement processes within all NSB HQ and its organizational elements staff members as well as NCISG HQ and other NSBs if requested.

Ø Submits observations in his/her area of expertise and contributes to the Lessons Learned process.

Ø Under Senior Contracting Officer supervision authorized to negotiate contracts subject to approval.

postings.organisation: Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA)
postings.description:
The post is budgeted from 1 January 2027, and the successful candidate is expected to start employment as soon as possible thereafter.

1. OVERVIEW OF DIANA

NATO DIANA is the Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic, a NATO body dedicated to finding and accelerating innovation to provide decisive defence and security effects for the Alliance, while fostering deep-tech innovation.

NATO DIANA is comprised of a Board of Directors, representing all 32 nations, and an operational team referred to as the DIANA Executive (“DX”). Operating from three offices in Europe and North America, the DX leverages a network of military end users, world-leading accelerator sites, test centres, professional mentors and experts, and Allied expertise to accelerate the most innovative technologies from across the NATO Alliance. DIANA is a dynamic, agile workplace, which strives for innovative thinking, diversity, and performance excellence across all teams. To achieve our mission, DIANA is committed to providing our people with an environment that is positive, inclusive and collaborative.

2. OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE

The Commercial Operations Officer operates at the intersection of strategy, market intelligence, and data analytics to assess growth opportunities for DIANA innovators, emerging technology trends, and defence sector demand signals. This role requires ownership of insight generation to directly influence how DIANA supports growth and market opportunities for its innovators.

*Reserve candidates may be considered for similar posts in Estonia or UK, if appropriate. *

Reporting to the Chief Adoption Officer or their delegate.

Duties of this role include:

- Provide forward-looking perspectives on emerging technology markets and trends.

- Integrate internal and external data sources to identify patterns, trends, strategic insights, and competitive opportunities for DIANA innovators.

- Conduct market research and analysis to understand defence customer demand and map commercial solutions able to solve Allied defence problems.

- Identify opportunities to improve data quality and collection across teams to inform how DIANA delivers growth support for innovators.

- Prepare executive briefings, market assessments, competitive analysis, and strategic presentations for senior leadership.

- Perform any other related duties as may be required.

3. ROLE REQUIREMENTS, QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

ESSENTIAL

The incumbent must have:

- A Bachelor’s degree from a nationally recognised/certified university in business, marketing, economics or a related field, together with at least two years of relevant professional experience; or, exceptionally, at least six years of progressive relevant professional experience in lieu of a degree.

- A minimum of two years of relevant professional experience in market research and analysis, business intelligence, commercial insights, data analytics or a related field.

- Demonstrated experience using business intelligence tools, such as Power BI or Tableau, and Python-based analytics or automation to analyse and present data.

- Demonstrated experience translating market research, commercial insights or technology assessments into evidence-based recommendations that support strategy development, portfolio management or growth initiatives for emerging technologies or start-ups.

- Proven ability to conduct quantitative analysis, interpret complex datasets and communicate clear, actionable insights to support organisational decision-making.

- Possess the following minimum proficiency levels in NATO’s official languages (English and French): Level V (“Advanced”) in one language and Level I (“Beginner”) in the other.

NOTE: Most of DIANA’s internal work is conducted in the English language.

DESIRABLE

The following would be considered an advantage:

- A Master’s degree in business, economics, data analytics, technology management or another relevant field.

- Knowledge of defence, security, dual-use or emerging-technology markets and ecosystems.

- Experience producing concise, evidence-based insights for senior leaders while also undertaking the underlying data collection, validation and analysis.

COMPETENCIES

The incumbent must demonstrate:

- Organizational and Environmental Awareness: Understands the wider mission and considers the impact of their actions on others.

- Initiative & Responsibility: Takes ownership and accountability.

- Adaptability & Flexibility: Embraces change, adjusts priorities as needed, and continues to deliver results in evolving environments.

- Customer Service Orientation: Provides timely, professional, and solution-focused support to all stakeholders.

- Planning & Prioritizing: Allocates time and resources effectively, balances competing priorities, and delivers work to agreed timelines.

- Teamwork: Collaborates openly and supports colleagues to achieve shared goals.

- Self-awareness and a Learning Mindset: Seeks opportunities to learn, reflects on experience, and applies learning to improve outcomes.

4. WHAT WE OFFER

- Genuinely meaningful work as part of the newest unit within the most successful alliance in history.

- Tax-free salary.

- Household and children’s allowances and privileges for expatriate staff including expatriation and educational allowances (where applicable) and additional home leave.

- Excellent private health insurance scheme.

- NATO pension scheme.

- Generous annual leave of 30 days plus official holidays.

- Flexible working conditions and a smoke-free office in Halifax.

- Opportunities for learning and development.

In accordance with the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations, the successful candidate will receive a definite duration contract of three years, which may be followed by an extension.

If the successful applicant is seconded from the national administration of one of NATO’s member States, a 3-year definite duration contract will be offered, which may be renewed for a further period of up to 3 years subject to the agreement of the national authority concerned. ** PENDING BUDGET APPROVAL **

1. SUMMARY

The Joint Intelligence and Security Division (JISD) has two main missions: to provide strategic intelligence to NATO HQ decision makers and to protect NATO’s personnel, information, and physical assets. JISD’s Intelligence pillar, comprised of both military and civilian personnel, is responsible for ensuring the situational awareness of the North Atlantic Council (NAC), the Military Committee (MC) and the senior-level decision-makers on strategic issues of concern. Its functional areas address intelligence analysis and production, intelligence policy, and intelligence capability development. JISD’s Security pillar is responsible for the overall coordination of NATO security among member Nations, NATO civil and military bodies as well as International Organizations and partner countries with which NATO cooperates. It is also responsible for the security of the NATO Headquarters (HQ), its personnel, information, physical assets, and for the protection of the Secretary General.
Within the Protective Security & Emergency Service Branch (PSESB), the incumbent, is responsible for ensuring the security of the construction sites as part of the HQ Adaptation Programme and all other related activities. More particularly, they will be responsible for enforcing construction security guidelines, organizing and supervising security measures, supporting security risk assessments, overseeing access control arrangements, conducting compliance checks, and coordinating with relevant stakeholders to maintain site security and compliance.
This position requires flexibility to work outside of normal working hours and travel occasionally, when requested.

2. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The incumbent must:
• possess a university degree in security management, project/programme management, engineering, construction management, facilities management, risk management, or another relevant field;
• have a minimum of 3 years’ relevant experience in construction security, physical security, security coordination/operations, or programme/project support in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment, preferably involving construction or infrastructure projects;
• have strong coordination and organizational skills, and the ability to manage security operations effectively;
• possess excellent writing and communication skills, and be able to draft clear and concise reports; and
• possess the following minimum levels in the official languages of NATO (English/ French): V (“Advanced”) in one and II (“Elementary”) in the other.

The following would be considered an advantage:
• extensive experience in drafting and implementing construction security plans;
• knowledge of information security principles, including need-to-know, access restrictions and the protection of sensitive or classified construction-related documentation; and
• familiarity with physical security systems, including access control, CCTV, intrusion detection and perimeter protection.

Adjust plans and respond to changes in requirements in a positive and flexible manner.

Stakeholder Management: Ensure effective cooperation and maintain interaction with internal and external stakeholders for the timely implementation of security regulations and procedures for which JIS/NOS/PSESB is responsible. Coordinate security requirements with contractors, sub-contractors and project stakeholders, including access control, security briefings, escort requirements, deliveries and compliance with site security procedures.

Perform any other related duty as assigned.

Interactions: The incumbent works and liaises closely with Workspace Management and Business Continuity (WMBC), teams supporting the HQ – Adaptation programme, PSESB, and other JISD branches and units, such as the JISD Enterprise & Divisional Coherence Unit, for day-to-day matters. - Conceptual Thinking: sees patterns based on life/work experience.

- Customer Service Orientation: takes personal responsibility for correcting problems.

1. Post Context/Post Summary
Allied Land Command (LANDCOM) HQ is the Theatre Land Component and Land Advocate responsible for coordinating and synchronizing NATO and Partner Land Forces by enabling land domain readiness, interoperability, standardization, and competency; on order deploys headquarters elements to provide planning, coordination, and command capabilities to Allied forces.
The Support Directorate is responsible for providing LANDCOM with organizational structures, personnel, logistics, communications and information systems and base support.
The G6 Cyberspace Division plans and monitors the provision of communication and information services by the NATO CIS Agency (NCIA) to LANDCOM, it also plans and executes Communications and Information Systems infrastructure and defensive cyberspace operations.
The Data Scientist (AI) is responsible for managing all data and data-related functions, enabling LANDCOM to make data-driven decisions. This includes managing data strategies, analytical processes, governance procedures, data protection requirements, and information dissemination.

2. Principal Duties
The incumbent's duties are:
• Prioritizing data security and privacy
• Enhancing real-time analytics capabilities
• Establishing a robust data governance framework
• Scaling cloud and hybrid solutions
• Accelerating AI and machine learning integration
• Building a data-driven culture
• Adopting emerging technologies
• Supporting internal and external analysts, helping to maintain the Agency’s data stores and tools to process, analyse and learn from this data;
• Executes processes and procedures related to data engineering, including those for data pipelines;
• Supports the maintenance of the Agency’s data lakes, implementing updates and working with system owners to ensure data is available for analysis;
• Contributes to the design and updates to the Agency’s data lakes, and data science approaches, in conjunction with the data science team and Service Line analysts;
• Contributes to the machine learning initiative across the Agency with suggestions for ML approaches and implementation, including the processing of training data and performance assessment of machine learning techniques on datasets;
• In conjunction with the Data Science Team, manage and update the Agency toolset for data analysis;
• Contributes to new/modifications to data science toolsets and metrics, and to machine learning toolsets and metrics.

3. Special Requirements and Additional Duties
The employee may be required to perform a similar range of duties elsewhere within the organization at the same grade without there being any change to the contract.
The incumbent may be required to undertake operation deployments in support of military operations and exercises and/or TDY assignments both within and without NATO's boundaries. Such operational requirement may exceed 30 days duration up to 183 days in any period of 547 days, and may be on short notice. For NATO International Civilian Staff, acceptance of an employment contract linked to this post constitutes agreement to deploy in excess of 30 days if required.
The work is normally performed in a Normal NATO office working environment.
Normal Working Conditions apply.
The risk of injury is categorized as No Risk.

4. Essential Qualifications
a. Professional/Experience
(1) Data Engineering
Designing, building, operationalizing, securing and monitoring distributed data infrastructures. Data engineers are managing, optimizing, overseeing and monitoring data retrieval, storage and distribution as well as preparing data for analytical or operational use to enable data driven decision-making. The identification of data sources, processing concepts and methods and their translation into a coherent design, with a particular emphasis on security and compliance; scalability and efficiency; reliability and fidelity; and flexibility and portability. Data infrastructures (pipelines and stores) must be compatible with the overarching IT architectures, and adhere to legislative and corporate policies. Data engineers harvest both structured and unstructured data sets from different sources systems; integrating, consolidating and cleansing data; and structuring and storing it for use for predictive analytics, machine learning and data mining purposes. Data engineering requires a solid conceptual understanding of Data architecture, data models, relational and non-relational database design, query execution and optimization, artificial intelligence, machine learning models and logical operations.
Skill Level (Enable)
Designs data pipelines and stores using appropriate modelling techniques following agreed architectures, design standards, data engineering patterns and methodology. Identifies and evaluates alternative design options and trade-offs. Creates multiple design views to address the concerns of the different stakeholders and to handle both functional and non-functional requirements. Builds reference data sets and models, simulates or prototypes the behaviour and quality of proposed data engineering solutions to enable approval by stakeholders. Delivers and maintains data engineering solutions. Reviews, verifies and improves own designs against original requirements.
Experience
At least four years’ experience in data engineering and CIS systems design at a major CIS company.
(2) Enterprise IT governance
The establishment and oversight of an organization’s approach to the use of Information systems and digital services, and associated technology, in line with the needs of the principal stakeholders of the organization and overall organizational corporate governance requirements. The determination and accountability for evaluation of current and future needs; directing the planning for both supply and demand of these services; the quality, characteristics, and level of IT services; and for monitoring the conformance to obligations (including regulatory, legislation, control, and other standards) to ensure positive contribution of IT to the organization’s goals and objectives.

Skill Level (Enable)
Works under general direction within a clear framework of accountability. Exercises substantial personal responsibility and autonomy. Plans own work to meet given objectives and processes. Influences customers, suppliers and partners at account level. May have some responsibility for the work of others and for the allocation of resources. Participates in external activities related to own specialism. Makes decisions which influence the success of projects and team objectives. Work includes a broad range of complex technical or professional activities, in a variety of contexts. Investigates, defines and resolves complex issues. Selects appropriately from applicable standards, methods, tools and applications. Communicates fluently, orally and in writing, and can present complex information to both technical and non-technical audiences. Facilitates collaboration between stakeholders who share common objectives. Plans, schedules and monitors work to meet time and quality targets. Rapidly absorbs new information and applies it effectively. Maintains an awareness of developing technologies and their application and takes some responsibility for driving own development.
Experience
Four years’ experience in the determination of current and future CIS needs and in monitoring the performance of CIS systems in a large organization.
b. Education/Training
University Degree in computer science, engineering disciplines, statistics or similar numerate discipline, operations research, information technology, information systems engineering, business administration, quality engineering or related discipline and 2 years function related experience, or Higher Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training in that discipline leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 4 years post related experience.

Experience (5-10 years) leading major Information and Communication Technology (ICT) transformation programs at the senior executive management level, involving leading and managing change in a dynamic technical organization. Such experience should encompass:
• Managing and overseeing the lifecycle of data, including collection, storage, and dissemination

• Ensuring the safe collection and dissemination of data according to data protection laws and governance policies

The Joint Force Training Centre supports Warfare Development, contributing to concept development and maintenance of joint doctrine and standards while coordinating the integration of experimentation, capability development, and interoperability to improve NATO’s interoperability, capabilities, and operational effectiveness.

The Training and Exercise Enabling Division (TEED) enables training and exercises, and warfare development events. Likewise, the Division provides the basis for the Joint Force Training Centre’s engagement with Allied Command Transformation Doctrine validation activities. The Division also maintains the JFTC’s analysis and lessons learned capability for both training/exercise/experimentation and institutional improvement.

The Command, Control, Communications & Computers and Modeling and Simulation (C4/MS) Branch ensures availability of the JFTC technical platform in support of the JFTC core business and Programme of Work (POW), to include communications and exercise support systems at JFTC and in support of the execution of static and distributed as well as single- and multi-echelon training, exercises, tests and experiments.

The Modeling and Simulation Section (MS) Section is responsible for Computer Assisted Exercise (CAX) and simulation support to combined and joint, single and multi-echelon training and exercises in a static or distributed environment for tactical and operational-level headquarters, staffs, and forces across the full spectrum of Alliance operations; and, supports testing and experimentation. This includes planning for the maintenance and improvement of the technical environment, and the delivery of the CAX infrastructure.

The incumbent is a Wargaming Database specialist, supporting the MS Section in all wargaming simulation aspects.

Reports to: Section Head (M&S) - OF-3

Principal Duties:

The incumbent’s duties are:

a. Creates, manages and modifies Computer Assisted Wargaming (CAW) databases for CAW exercises and any other NATO 2030 Agenda activities supported by JFTC.

c. Leads the database development process in coordination with wargaming event planners.

d. Liaises with the wargaming team and the training audience for parameter input, to ensure database accuracy.

h. Leads wargaming database review and validation sessions with wargaming planners and force providers.

i. Co-ordinates with systems engineers – wargaming planners, the conduct of wargaming database validation sessions.

k. Monitors simulation during the CAW events and implements coordinated modifications.

l. Maintains a library of CAW databases of units and performance parameters.

m. Assists in the documentation of CAW databases as required by training audiences and exercise control staff.

n. Co-ordinates the CAW database requirements and tool developments with modelling and simulation service providers.

o. Co-ordinates with systems engineers – wargaming planners on the use of new releases of simulations.

p. Provides wargaming planning support to event project teams.

q. Acts as the knowledge base within JFTC for wargaming databases-related issues in support of NATO 2030 activities.

Decision Authority - Authorized to make decisions regarding the work priorities of supporting staff assigned to specified initiatives. Normal Working Conditions apply.

3) Four years’ experience in developing technical policy level documents.

postings.description:
1. SUMMARY

The Defence Industry, Innovation and Armaments Division (D2IA) leads on the rapid development and delivery of cutting-edge and interoperable defence capabilities, working with innovation ecosystems and industry across the Alliance to meet NATO’s deterrence and defence needs.
The incumbent works in the Industry, Partnerships and Policy Section (IPPS), and carries out the duties of a defence production analyst within a team of defence industrial capacity officers. The incumbent is responsible for applying analytical techniques to the collection and analysis of data from all relevant sources on defence industrial capacity and production. Additionally, the incumbent supports the development of analytical products and provides actionable recommendations, in support of IPPS and overall D2IA work strands.

2. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The incumbent must:
• possess a university degree or equivalent level qualification in a relevant field;
• have at least 2 years of relevant work experience, including researching, analysing and presenting data for strategic decision making, using qualitative and quantitative research methods;
• have an understanding of current strategic policies and issues relating to the transatlantic defence and technological industrial base;
• have excellent analytical skills, strong briefing (verbal and written) skills including the ability to identify and distil complex policy issues; and
• possess the following minimum levels of NATO’s official languages (English/French): V (“Advanced”) in one; I (“Beginner”) in the other.

Information Management: Develop and oversee data repositories, resources and tools to support the section’s efficient access to information in relation to industrial production and supply chains. Monitor ongoing developments related to the Alliance’s industrial base. Exchange knowledge and information with colleagues on topics influenced by industrial developments.

Project Management: Identify, analyse, design and contribute expertise to projects/programmes. Deliver high quality reports on defence industrial matters as tasked, including actionable recommendations based on an assessment of available information. Identify and analyse trends related insights to inform decision-making.

postings.title: Engineer (Digital Infrastructure)
postings.description:
NCIA exists for one reason: to ensure the Alliance can communicate securely and reliably, whether in critical political consultations or during complex military operations. We are a key enabler of NATO's core mission to keep one billion people safe.

Our technology and cyber experts power NATO's digital capabilities, from data-driven decision-making and secure networks to resilient operations and mission execution across land, air, sea, cyber and space domains.

This mission is made possible by our people. We are a team of around 3,500 civilian and military staff working across 30 locations throughout Europe and North America.

To meet growing operational demand, the Directorate of CIS Support Units (DCSU) is expanding its presence across a number of locations. DCSU manages, delivers and maintains communications and information systems products and services for NATO customers.

Through its CIS Support Units, DCSU provides the vital connection between customers and NCIA's wider service-delivery organisation.

This role will provide direct, on-site infrastructure and customer support to remote NATO offices in Kyiv. The assignment combines hands-on digital infrastructure engineering, information security, local IT support, logistics, cryptographic coordination and management of service-based contracts.

About the Role

As Digital Infrastructure Engineer, you will design, implement, operate and improve the server, storage, data-centre and cloud-related infrastructure supporting remote NATO offices in Kyiv. You will provide on-site IT support, troubleshoot infrastructure issues, maintain system software and storage services, and help ensure that local digital services remain secure, resilient and reliable. Working with users, CSU Brussels, specialist support teams, suppliers and other technical organisations, you will coordinate integrations, security controls, network support and service-based contracts. The role is expected to spend approximately 75% of its time in Kyiv, operating on a recurring pattern of six weeks in Kyiv followed by two weeks in Brussels. The post does not directly supervise staff but does require oversight of external contractors.

What You Will Do

· Design, install, configure and maintain server, storage, system-software and related infrastructure services.

· Develop system designs, integration plans, test environments and detailed technical specifications in line with agreed architectures and standards.

· Monitor infrastructure load, performance, availability and security events, and take corrective or proactive action where required.

· Carry out system-software maintenance, backup and restore activity, storage management and routine administration using approved tools and scripts.

· Provide on-site IT support, network-equipment support, IT logistics and incident escalation for remote NATO offices.

· Apply information-security controls, perform risk and business-impact analysis, and support investigation of suspected attacks or security incidents.

· Support and coordinate cryptographic activities in accordance with NATO requirements.

· Manage service-based contracts associated with the remote site, monitor supplier performance and support contract renewal activity.

How You Will Contribute

Everything starts with the customer and the user. You will be expected to understand local requirements, maintain direct engagement and take ownership for reliable technical outcomes.

You will work across organisational and geographic boundaries, connecting local users with CSU Brussels, support teams, suppliers and technical specialists.

You will also be expected to act with sound judgement, initiative and appropriate pace in a demanding operating environment, while complying with applicable NATO security measures and procedures.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for candidates who meet the technical and professional requirements of the post and who can demonstrate:

· A strong focus on customer and user needs

· Ownership, initiative and accountability

· Sound judgement and practical problem-solving

· Effective collaboration across organisational and geographic boundaries

· The ability to work independently and productively in a remote-site environment

· A disciplined approach to security, risk and service reliability

· Adaptability and commitment to delivering results in demanding circumstances

Essential Education and Experience

· A bachelor's degree in a related discipline with 2 years of post-related experience, or at least 6 years of extensive and progressive post-related experience where the degree requirement is exceptionally compensated.

· At least 2 years of practical experience designing, implementing and managing technology, software and hardware supporting servers, storage systems, data centres or cloud services.

· Practical experience troubleshooting infrastructure-related issues and performing regular maintenance.

· Good communication and interpersonal skills.

· Good analytical skills and a solution-oriented approach.

· A thorough knowledge of one NATO language, both written and spoken; some knowledge of the other is desirable.

Desirable Education and Experience

· At least 1 year of experience providing IT support in conflict zones.

· A current certificate of attendance for hostile-environment awareness training.

· At least 1 year of experience communicating with users at all levels, including senior or VIP users.

· NATO cryptographic certifications.

· Knowledge of Ukrainian and/or Russian.

Important Information Before Applying

· The primary duty location is Kyiv, Ukraine. Brussels, Belgium is identified as the other location for the post.

· Kyiv as an extreme-risk location rated by the NATO Office of Security. Special security measures will apply to personnel assigned to or travelling to the location.

· Family members will not be relocated with the successful candidate.

· The assignment is expected to spend approximately 75% of overall time in Kyiv, using a recurring pattern of six weeks in Kyiv followed by two weeks in Brussels.

· The role may require on-demand support outside normal business hours and work on site.

· Candidates should not make assumptions about benefits, allowances, relocation support or other location-specific entitlements. Information about applicable conditions will be provided only when formally confirmed.

· Any selection or appointment will remain subject to all required organisational, legal, administrative, host-nation, financial, security and employment requirements.

· Progression through the recruitment process does not constitute a firm offer of appointment.

How to Apply

Please review the complete Job Description before submitting your application.

Applicants must demonstrate how they meet the essential requirements of the post and complete the prescreening questions included in the application.

Post Context

ACT contributes to preserving the peace, security and territorial integrity of Alliance member states by leading, at Strategic Command level, Warfare Development required to enhance NATO’s posture, military structures, forces, capabilities and doctrines.

The Capability Development Directorate (CAPDEV) comprises two Divisions—Requirements and Capabilities. The Directorate supports SACT in his Capabilities Requirement Authority (CRA) role. It is responsible for a holistic through lifecycle Capability Development approach that infuses innovation and transformative efforts that are an integral part of the Warfare Development. This includes responsibilities for elicitation, development, capture and collection, quality review, traceability and visibility of capability requirements.

The Requirements Division executes requirements management for NATO capabilities. It develops capability requirements, provides traceability and quality assurance of capability requirements, performs gap analysis and supports interoperability and implementation options across the DOTMLPFI spectrum.

The Federated Interoperability Branch supports and enables the delivery of coherent and interoperable capabilities by developing and verifying the associated capability specifications in order to ensure Day Zero interoperability of people, processes, and technologies

The Interoperability Delivery Section leads the Interoperability, Verification and Validation (IV&V) of C2 Interoperability solutions implemented in NATO and national systems, mainly through the Coalition Warrior Interoperability Exercise and Coalition Interoperability and Assurance Validation, but increasingly through other test activities that will eventually provide a continual, year-round testing environment. postings.description:
CMRE is looking for applicants to establish a pool of candidates for temporary positions that may arise within the Engineering and Information Technology Division (EITD) at NATO STO-CMRE, La Spezia, Italy.

Are you a national of a NATO member state, at the beginning of your professional career, with practical technical skills in engineering, electronics, information technology, systems support, data acquisition, mechanical or marine engineering, oceanographic systems, unmanned systems, laboratory support or field/at-sea technical activities? Then this may be an opportunity for you!

These temporary positions are aimed primarily at technicians, junior engineers and early-career professionals who are interested in supporting maritime research and experimentation activities in a hands-on technical environment.

In view of the nature and of the urgency of the temporary positions we are looking to fill, it is important for candidates to be available for temporary employment on short notice. In practice, this implies either being in possession of valid NATO security clearance at the time of application, or having been in possession of such a clearance with the possibility to reactivate it swiftly. We therefore only encourage applications for temporary positions if you are already, or have previously been, in possession of a valid NATO security clearance.

1. POST CONTEXT

These positions are within the Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE), an Organisation of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

CMRE is an established, world-class scientific research and experimentation facility that organizes and conducts scientific research and technology development, centred on the maritime domain, to deliver innovative, field-tested Science & Technology solutions addressing the defence and security needs of the Alliance.

The positions are within the Engineering and Information Technology Division (EITD).

EITD consists of the Engineering Branch and the Information Technology Branch.

The Engineering Branch supports the engineering and technological requirements of the Centre’s research activities by designing, developing, integrating, testing, maintaining, repairing and calibrating electronic, oceanographic, mechanical, acoustic, unmanned and related systems, including prototypes and limited-production systems.

The Information Technology Branch supports computing, networking, data infrastructure, software applications, IT services, interoperability, security and compliance with relevant NATO policies and regulations.

Temporary staff may be assigned to support one or more EITD activities depending on operational needs, qualifications and experience.

2. PRINCIPAL DUTIES

The selected candidates may be required to perform one or more of the following duties, under the supervision of experienced staff:

Engineering Systems Support

- Support assembly, integration, testing and maintenance of engineering systems;

- Assist laboratory, workshop, field and shipboard equipment operation;

- Troubleshoot, repair, calibrate and check technical systems;

- Prepare equipment for trials, exercises, experiments and demonstrations;

- Integrate sensors, payloads, cables, interfaces and acquisition equipment;

- Configure, test and validate embedded or automation systems;

- Prepare, maintain and test unmanned maritime systems;

- Support deployment, recovery and safe marine equipment handling;

- Collect, log and quality-check basic technical data;

- Maintain records on configuration, testing, maintenance and use.

Information Technology and Systems Support

- System administration;

- Asset management;

- Security Compliance;

- Quality Assurance.

General Administrative Technical Support

- Prepare basic documentation, equipment records, checklists and test notes;

- Assist with technical reports, trial records and configuration documents;

- Support inventory, procurement follow-up and experiment logistics;

- Provide accurate, timely information for team coordination.

3. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

a) Education / Experience

- Higher vocational training in a relevant discipline with 1 year post-related experience.

Or

- Higher secondary educational qualification with 3 years post-related experience.

Relevant disciplines may include, but are not limited to:

- Electronics;

- Telecommunications;

- Mechanical, marine, ocean or mechatronics engineering;

- Automation and control;

- Robotics or unmanned systems;

- Technical laboratory, workshop or field support;

- IT.

b) Professional Experience

You will have practical experience in one or more of the following areas:

- Technical support in a laboratory, workshop, field or shipboard environment;

- Electronics, cabling, sensors, data acquisition or embedded systems;

- Mechanical, electro-mechanical, marine or oceanographic systems;

- Unmanned systems, acoustic systems, sonar or marine sensors;

- Equipment maintenance, testing, calibration, configuration or documentation;

- Asset tracking, inventory or technical administrative support;

- Administration and IT process support

c) Language Requirements

A thorough knowledge of one of the two NATO official languages (written and spoken) is essential and some knowledge of the other is desirable.

English SLP 3333 (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing).

NOTE: Most of the work at CMRE is conducted in English.

4. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND ADDITIONAL DUTIES

a) Flexibility Clause

The incumbent may be required to perform other related duties as directed.

All other related duties should correspond with the required competencies for the job.

b) Deployment/Travel

The incumbent may be required to undertake TDY assignments within and outside NATO boundaries.

The incumbent may be required to perform their duties onboard Centre or chartered vessels.

Depending on the assignment, candidates may be required to obtain or hold a fit-for-sea certificate in line with applicable International Maritime Organisation and International Labour Organisation requirements.

5. DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

Depending on the assignment, the following would be considered an advantage:

Engineering Systems Support

- Experience in research, maritime, defence or multinational technical environments.

- Experience supporting sea trials, experiments, demonstrations or technical exercises.

- Ability to read drawings, wiring diagrams, specifications and procedures.

- Experience using test equipment, tools, workbenches or calibration equipment.

- Experience supporting electronic, mechanical, marine or sensor systems.

- Experience with sensors, payloads, cables, interfaces or acquisition equipment.

- Experience supporting testing, calibration, maintenance, configuration or deployment.

- Experience supporting unmanned maritime systems and payload integration.

- Experience with CAD, prototyping, manufacturing, automation or control systems.

- Experience supporting data collection, logging, quality checks or documentation.

IT and Systems Support

- Experience in Administration and IT process support;

- Asset management;

- System administration;

- Cloud computing.

Education

- A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent technical qualification in a relevant discipline would be an advantage, but is not mandatory where the candidate has relevant practical experience.

Languages

- Knowledge of French or Italian would be an advantage.

6. COMPETENCIES

The successful candidate should possess the following competencies and personal attributes:

- Delivering Results & Meeting Customer Expectations: Completes assigned tasks accurately, efficiently and within agreed deadlines. Understands customer needs and provides practical, service-oriented support.

- Following Instructions & Procedures: understands and follows established instructions, rules, and procedures accurately and consistently. Seeks clarification when needed and respects organisational processes;

- Working with people: works constructively with colleagues and contributes positively to team objectives;

- Learning & Developing: is willing to develop new technical skills and learn from experienced staff.

- Relating & Networking: Establishes good relationships with customers and colleagues; relates well to people at all levels.

All CMRE personnel are expected to conduct themselves in accordance with the current NATO Code of Conduct agreed by the North Atlantic Council (NAC), and thus display the core values of integrity, impartiality, loyalty, accountability, and professionalism.

7. REMARKS

The duties are performed in an office, laboratory, workshop, field environment or onboard Centre vessels.

___________________________

What we offer:

- 37.5 hours per week schedule.
- 2.5 paid days of leave per month.
- A world class research facility located in the sea port of La Spezia, Italy supported by two specialised research vessels.

- An exciting place in which to work situated at an ideal location, the port of La Spezia, Italy, enabling synergy with regional and global academic institutes and industry.

- Contract: in accordance with NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations, temporary staff may not be employed more than 6 months for the same assignment. However, if later required, contracts may be extended for another period up to six months.

- Salary: the remuneration of temporary personnel will be specified in their contracts. It is not exempt from taxation. Temporary personnel are responsible for acquitting themselves of their responsibilities for the payment of taxes.

- Benefits package: temporary staff are covered by a benefit package which consists of pension contributions by the Organisation (12% of basic salary), medical and accident benefits (death and invalidity) provided under the NATO Group insurance contract, and paid leave of 2.5 days per month worked.

Our recruitment process:

- Please note that we can only accept applications from nationals of NATO member countries.

- Applications (including the most relevant publications, the diplomas - stating the highest level of education - and a CV) for this vacancy are to be submitted using the E-recruitment system (NATO Taleo).

- You are responsible for keeping your information up-to-date by making the appropriate changes (e.g. availability, clearance, etc.) directly in your Taleo application. Please do not re-apply if changes occur, but edit your application at any time.

- When submitting your application, please note that you are applying to a candidate pool, and not for a particular assignment. You will receive an acknowledgement of receipt of your application from the system. The application does not constitute a guarantee of employment.

- Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance (provided by the national Authorities of the selected candidate) and approval of the candidate’s medical file by the CMRE Medical Adviser.

- It is a condition of employment that before a temporary staff member can be appointed, the Organization must have received a security clearance certificate (minimum NATO Secret) from the government of the country or countries of which they are nationals.

- Any questions on this subject should be sent to recruitment@cmre.nato.int.

Additional information:

- CMRE values diverse backgrounds and perspectives and is committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and talented workforce. We welcome applications of nationals from all Member States and strongly encourage women to apply.

- Selected candidates are expected to be role models of integrity, and to promote good governance through ongoing efforts in their work.

1. SUMMARY

The Joint Intelligence and Security Division (JISD) has two main missions: to provide strategic intelligence to NATO HQ decision makers and to protect NATO’s personnel, information, and physical assets. JISD’s Intelligence pillar, comprised of both military and civilian personnel, is responsible for ensuring the situational awareness of the North Atlantic Council (NAC), the Military Committee (MC) and the senior-level decision-makers on strategic issues of concern. Its functional areas address intelligence analysis and production, intelligence policy, and intelligence capability development. JISD’s Security pillar is responsible for the overall coordination of NATO security among member Nations, NATO civil and military bodies as well as International Organizations and partner countries with which NATO cooperates. It is also responsible for the security of the NATO Headquarters (HQ), its personnel, information, physical assets, and for the protection of the Secretary General.
Within JISD’s Security pillar, the NATO Office of Security (NOS) is responsible for the overall coordination of NATO security among diverse NATO bodies and personnel, abroad or at the Headquarters (HQ), and other partnering International Organisations.
The Executive Driver is responsible for supporting the Office of the Secretary General in its daily operations. The incumbent is responsible for successfully carrying out authorized missions using the Organizations' official vehicles according to NATO protocol. The incumbent will also be responsible for handling various administrative and maintenance actions linked to the daily tasks.
The incumbent will be required to work outside normal office hours at short notice and be assigned on call duties, when required.

2. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The incumbent must:
• have an educational background, equivalent to higher secondary level;
• have 3 years of experience as a professional VIP driver working for organisations with high-ranking civilians/military commanders or high-level governmental institutions;
• hold a driving license for B (normal vehicles) and C (vehicles >3.5 T) categories, according to Belgian regulations;
• possess a valid medical certificate, or willingness to review it, allowing the driving of heavy transport; and
• possess the following minimum levels of NATO’s official languages (English/French): V (“Advanced”) in one; III (“Intermediate”) in the other.

The following would be considered an advantage:
• knowledge of and certification in advanced driving skills and a first-aid/BLS-AED certificate provided by a recognized school or institution;
• experienced knowledge of road infrastructure in Brussels, Belgium and surrounding countries; and
• been an active member of a Close Protection Team of a NATO member
nation’s security or intelligence service, armed forces or of their civilian/military police.

3. MAIN ACCOUNTABILITIES

Planning and Execution: Plan and execute transportation tasks for the NATO senior leadership primarily in Brussels, Belgium but also occasionally in neighbouring cities and countries. Drive armoured and non-armoured passenger cars and vans, on official NATO business, following protocol and adhering to organizational priorities. Calculate driving times and distances, determining approximate arrival times. Carry out any other official transport tasks. Assist colleagues in the simple maintenance of NATO official vehicles.

Information Management: Create and file daily logs, joint accident reports, trip sheets and any other documents required. Handle all work related to the transport of documents from NATO Headquarters to and from Embassies and Ministries carried out by the Transport Service.

Expertise Development: Take part in defensive/offensive driving courses and attend any training course identified by the CPU management as being essential to accomplish the tasks/missions.

Stakeholder Management: Work in a team to ensure that the official driving needs of the Organization are met. Deal tactfully, politely and discreetly with passengers. Assist colleagues with administrative, maintenance and dispatch work as needed.

Perform any other related duty as assigned.

4. INTERRELATIONSHIPS

Reporting line: Through the daily management of a Program Coordinator, the incumbent reports to the Head, CPU.
Interactions: The incumbent coordinates arrangements with the relevant staff in the Office of the Secretary General. The incumbent collaborates regularly with her/his team members.

Direct reports: N/A
Indirect reports: N/A

The incumbent will demonstrate:
• Achievement: works to meet standards.
• Customer Service Orientation: takes personal responsibility for correcting problems.
• Flexibility: accepts the need for flexibility.
• Initiative: reacts to short-term opportunities of problems.
• Organizational Commitment: models loyalty.
• Self-Control: responds calmly.
• Teamwork: cooperates.

Contract to be offered to the successful applicant (if non-seconded): Definite duration contract of three years’ duration; possibility of an indefinite duration contract thereafter.

Contract clause applicable:
In accordance with the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations, the successful candidate will receive a definite duration contract of three years, which may be followed by an indefinite duration contract.

postings.description:
Who we are:

For more than 70 years, NATO’s mission has been to preserve peace and security in the Alliance for nearly one billion citizens. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) and its predecessors have worked tirelessly in providing the means that enable the connectedness and togetherness that keep our Alliance strong. We are the NCIA, a team of 3000 civilian and military staff in 29 locations throughout Europe, North America and Asia.

Our technology and cyber experts allow NATO to conduct critical operations, protect NATO’s airspace, make data-driven decisions, defend against cyber-attacks, secure NATO networks and maintain superiority in space. This is all possible because of our greatest force, our people. In order to keep this edge we aim to hire, train and retain the very best staff.

Our staff members represent both the diversity and unity of our Alliance. When you join the NCIA, you will be part of an organization where you can contribute authentically to the mission and purpose of NATO and help us keep our technological edge.

About the job:
