postings.description:
- SUBJECT TO THE BGX BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND FUNDING APPROVAL-

1. SUMMARY

The BICES Group Executive (BGX), a NATO entity, is the executive body of the BICES Group (BG). The BG exists to enable the sharing and exchange of intelligence and information between and amongst NATO nations, with NATO, and with other non-NATO nations and organisations. Under the leadership of the Director, BGX is composed of the Intelligence and Enterprise Services (IES) Division, the Programme, Engineering and Maintenance (PEM) Division, the Operations and Security Services (OSS) Division, and the Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Cell.

The Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Cell acts as the executive arm of the BICES ISR community. It coordinates the development of an integrated multinational federated ISR Processing, Exploitation and Dissemination capability and enables coherent national, NATO and multinational ISR support to operations by ensuring interoperability, technical and procedural alignment, information flow coherence and collective readiness. The Cell maintains ISR documentation, governance artefacts, interoperability frameworks, reference resources and ISR information required to support participating nations and NATO entities in ISR integration and capability development. It further supports ISR exercises, trials, multinational readiness activities and contributes to long-term ISR evolution.

Under the supervision of the Head, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Cell, and in coordination with the ISR Lead Architect/Engineer, the incumbent administers and provides technical support for ISR services deployed on BICES. As an authorised BGX System Administrator, the incumbent maintains a functional dependency with the BGX Operational Authority and applies approved security and operational requirements when administering ISR systems within the BGX Element and Central Node.

The work is performed in a secure facility where slightly undesirable conditions may apply and involves a light risk of injury. The incumbent participates in the provision of continuous technical support and may be required to undertake on-call and overtime duties outside regular working hours.

Operational travel may be required in accordance with the BG Deployment Policy and national requirements.

2. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

Essential

The incumbent must:

- possess a technical degree or equivalent qualification in information systems management, library science, computer science, information science or a related discipline;

- have at least 6 years of professional experience as a Systems Administrator with background in both Microsoft Windows and Linux platforms;

- have proven experience with the installation, support, configuration and troubleshooting of IT services;

- be able to understand, assess and solve technical issues in a troubleshooting environment under pressure and with time constraints;

- have a demonstrated experience as system administrator in Microsoft/LINUX (MS WS SVR 2016 or above, RHEL 7.5 or above), HyperV and VMware environment, to include experience with maintaining Oracle and SQL Databases;

- have a demonstrated experience with VMware Horizon virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) environments, including the administration, maintenance and troubleshooting of Horizon-based virtual desktop services;

- have Microsoft Certifications in Server 2019 and Windows 10 (or above) and virtualization (e.g. VMware);

- have proven experience with storage, access, problem reporting and change control of Configuration Items (Cls);

- be willing to work outside of normal office working hours;

- possess level V (Advanced) of the English language.

Desirable

The following would be considered an advantage:

- recent experience providing ISR technical services support to military and coalition Operations;

- have proven experience with the installation, support, configuration and troubleshooting of ISR-related services, such as the Coalition Shared Dataserver (CSD);

- experience with ISR service interfaces between STANAG 4559 compliant systems and non-STANAG 4559 compliant ISR systems;

- experience with Information Exchange Gateway solutions supporting ISR service interfaces between different classification level networks;

- experience with status accounting and auditing, in line with recognized standards, such as ISO 9000, 9001 and 9004 throughout the ClS lifecycle;

- certification on Horizon (formerly VMware), version 7 or above;

- certification on IT industry/service provider standards, (e.g. ITIL);

- strong foundation in system security issues;

- French Level II (Elementary).

3. MAIN ACCOUNTABILITIES

Expertise Development

Maintain effective technical support for ISR services by assisting nations during capability fielding and testing activities. Provide technical advice and troubleshooting assistance for operational ISR services across approved classified and unclassified environments. Support change and release activities, including testing, rollout and rollback. Participate in Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity testing, record findings and contribute practical recommendations. Maintain current knowledge of technological developments relevant to the assigned work.

Information Management

Maintain accurate and current ISR technical and service documentation and ensure its controlled storage. Review and test ISR-related Standard Operating Procedures to support accurate and consistent application. Collect and report ISR system and service performance data to support service improvement. Provide technical input to reviews of service and support proposals. Support Service Improvement Plans and provide required information to the BGX Configuration Manager. Maintain configuration records for hardware and software installed for ISR functions and services.

Planning and Execution

Administer, operate and maintain assigned ISR systems and services, including STANAG 4559 Edition 4 Coalition Shared Data services, servers, databases, storage, backup and virtualisation environments. Install and configure approved hardware, software and application components in accordance with established procedures. Support testing of national implementations against approved BICES ISR reference tools and record the results. Resolve incidents and customer requests in coordination with the Service Desk, communications technicians, Information Assurance staff and the PEM Division. Provide first-, second- and third-level technical support as required. Implement approved upgrades, changes and modifications to ISR application services, including systems at the Alternate BICES Operations Centre. Monitor system utilisation, capacity and lifecycle status and report identified limitations.

Project Management

Support the timely execution of ISR-related projects and programmes within the assigned technical area. Contribute technical information to project schedules, testing and implementation activities. Coordinate assigned technical actions and report progress, risks, dependencies and deliverables to the responsible manager.

Stakeholder Management

Maintain effective working relationships with appropriate military and civilian officials in participating nations and NATO. Liaise with representatives of relevant scientific and industrial organisations in support of assigned technical activities. Cooperate with BGX Divisions on ISR-related security, event, incident, problem and configuration management activities.

4. INTERRELATIONSHIPS

The incumbent reports to the Head, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Cell. The incumbent coordinates with other BGX staff as required, particularly within the PEM and OSS Divisions, and works cooperatively with ISR Cell technicians.

Direct reports: None

Indirect reports: None

5. COMPETENCIES

Achievement

Works to meet expected performance standards and deliver outputs within agreed timelines. Applies diligence and accountability in maintaining ISR systems and resolving assigned technical issues.

Analytical Thinking

Breaks down problems and information to identify relationships, patterns and logical conclusions. Applies structured troubleshooting to identify the causes of ISR system and service problems.

Clarity and Accuracy

Communicates information in a clear and precise manner and checks work carefully for accuracy. Maintains reliable technical documentation, configuration records and test results.

Customer Service Orientation

Responds constructively to the needs and requests of internal and external users in support of service quality and mission needs. Provides timely and professional technical support to ISR users and stakeholders.

Initiative

Takes action within own area of responsibility to address issues and improve results without waiting to be told. Identifies technical or service issues and takes appropriate corrective action or refers them to the responsible authority.

Teamwork

Works cooperatively with others to achieve shared goals and supports a positive and collaborative team environment. Contributes effectively to ISR Cell technical activities and coordinated support across BGX.

6. CONTRACT

Contract to be offered to the successful applicant (if non-seconded): Definite duration contract of three years; possibility of renewal.

Contract clause applicable:

The successful applicant will be offered a 3-year definite duration contract, which may be renewed.

If the successful applicant is seconded from the national administration of one of NATO’s member States, a 3-year definite duration contract will be offered, which may be renewed, subject also to the agreement of the national authority concerned.

Serving staff will be offered a contract in accordance with the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations.

7. USEFUL INFORMATION REGARDING APPLICATION AND RECRUITMENT PROCESS

Please note that we can only accept applications from nationals of NATO member countries. Applications must be submitted using e-recruitment system, as applicable:

Before you apply to any position, we encourage you to click here and watch our video providing 6 tips to prepare you for your application and recruitment process.

postings.description:
POST CONTEXT/POST SUMMARY
Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) is a strategic military headquarters. Its role is to prepare, plan, conduct and execute NATO military operations, missions and tasks in order to achieve the strategic objectives of the Alliance. As such, it contributes to the deterrence of aggression and the preservation of peace, security, and the territorial integrity of Alliance. SHAPE supports the Supreme Allied Commander Europe in fulfilling his terms of reference, as directed by the North Atlantic- Council.

Within SHAPE, the Office of Legal Affairs (OLA) is responsible for providing legal advice and guidance to SACEUR, SHAPE staff, and the Legal Advisors of subordinated HQs in all relevant matters.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES
The Legal Executive Officer (LEXO)'s duties are:
 Executes the everyday management of the legal division and coordinates the work programme of the Division on behalf of the ACO Legal Advisor, issuing directions in this respect. Takes action, as required, on tasking and other assignments, coordinating with the OLA branch heads and other elements of OLA as appropriate.
 Manages the day-to-day operations and optimizes administrative processes of OLA. Ensures all deliverables are accurate and submitted consistently with deadlines, contributing to informed decision-making and strategic planning.
 Provides comprehensive support to the ACO Legal Advisor. Prepares briefing materials, conducts research, and drafts documents needed for meetings.
 Facilitates effective communication and coordination between the legal office and the Command Group and with other departments and commands within NATO. Facilitates the flow of direction and guidance from the ACO Legal Advisor to the OLA team and other legal offices. Attends and contributes to meetings, ensuring that legal office considerations are appropriately represented and addressed. Represents the ACO Legal Advisor in Boards, Meetings, or Committees.
 Assists the ACO Legal Advisor in executing Command Group orders, directives, and security regulations, guiding the team and ensuring enforcement and compliance across OLA members as necessary.
 Reviews all outgoing correspondence for quality and compliance with applicable directives and policies.
 Serves as or supervises the Divisional Security Officer and Fund Manager. Manages the computer and information systems and records management contractors to ensure effective performance, compliance, and alignment with organizational objectives.
 Ensures the proper archiving, classification, secure storage, and retrieval of all records in compliance with organizational policies, regulatory requirements, and document retention standards. Enables the use of the ACO Central Repository for International Agreements and other legal reference materials by SHAPE staff and ACO HQs.
 As tasked by the Director OLA, assists in handling legal matters within the office, supporting the Director OLA and the branch heads by investigating and examining relevant facts and legal questions, and providing recommendations for resolution.
 Drafts legal correspondence, directives, standard operating procedures, terms of reference, briefings, and other matters.
 Leads and optimizes ongoing projects, aligning stakeholder priorities, managing budgets, and driving innovation through effective implementation.
Supervisory Duties:
 Supervises the OLA civilian and military personnel responsible for supporting the above functions.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND ADDITIONAL DUTIES
The employee may be required to perform a similar range of duties elsewhere within the organization at the same grade without there being any change to the contract.

The Legal Executive Officer may be required to perform other related duties as directed (in particular, to serve as a member of Working Groups, Project Teams, etc. for defined periods of time). Additionally, she/he may be reassigned as directed by the Chief of Staff for up to 180 days (and when necessary, in excess of 180 days with her/his agreement).

Annual temporary duty (TDY) requirement: The incumbent may have to undertake TDY within and outside NATO’s boundaries and deployments may be required in support of military operations and exercises, and/or TDY assignments, for up to 30 days.

The incumbent may be required to work outside normal office hours.
The work is normally performed in a normal NATO office working environment.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS
a. Professional Experience
1) Previous experience in a coordination office/front office of an executive or general/flag officer official.
2) Previous managerial experience in a military headquarters or international organization.

b. Education/Training
University Degree in law or related discipline (e.g. business administration) or Higher Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training in that discipline leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 4 years post related experience.

c. Language
English - SLP 3333 (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS
a. Professional Experience
1) Additional years of experience in the areas described under essential qualifications above.
2) Sound knowledge of the NATO and ACO structure, organisation, and mission.
3) Previous experience in an executive officer function, to include managerial and supervising experience in a coordination office/front office of an executive or general/flag officer official.

b. Education/Training
1) Advanced degree in law.
2) Professional license to practice law or eligibility for the same.
3) Project manager training.

c. Language
French SLP 2222

ATTRIBUTES/COMPETENCIES
a. Personal attributes:
The incumbent must work collegially with and coordinate effectively with colleagues, including legal professionals and others, in an international environment. This requires the incumbent to show courtesy, empathy, negotiating skills, and service mindedness.

The incumbent must be capable of managing complex projects and prioritizing and assigning work effectively. This requires mental alertness, attention to details, and working well under pressure.

The incumbent must be capable of representing an executive-level official in interactions within the headquarters and with external organisations. This requires good interpersonal and communication skills, diplomacy, poise, and tact.

The incumbent must provide excellent customer service. This requires diligence, tact, and discretion (i.e., adherence to confidentiality).

The incumbent is expected to be capable of working with minimum supervision on routine matters.

Incumbent is expected to be capable of understanding and applying governing policies and procedures correctly to the execution of assigned responsibilities.

b. Professional Contacts:
Routinely, directly interrelates with members of the SHAPE staff and Command Group. Contacts, apart from SHAPE staff, are principally with legal support personnel in other NATO bodies, National Military Representatives to SHAPE, and national administrations of NATO and non-NATO countries in order to exchange information, to solicit information, to provide or seek guidance on various issues.

c. Supervisory duties:
Directly supervises and provides professional guidance and instruction to OLA staff responsible for supporting the functions described above.

REMARKS:
Duration of contract: Serving staff members will be offered a contract according to the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations (NCPR). Newly recruited staff will be offered a definite duration contract of three years normally followed by an indefinite duration contract.

The salary will be the basic entry-level monthly salary defined by the NATO Grade of the post, which may be augmented by allowances based on the selected staff member’s eligibility, and which is subject to the withholding of approximately 20% for pension and medical insurance contributions.

NATO is committed to diversity and inclusion, and strives to provide equal access to employment, advancement, and retention, independent of gender, age, nationality, ethnic origin, religion or belief, cultural background, sexual orientation, and disability. NATO welcomes applications of nationals from all member Nations.

As an employer, NATO values commitment to the principles of integrity, transparency, and accountability in accordance with international norms and practices established for the defence and related security sector. Selected candidates are expected to be role models of integrity, and to promote good governance through ongoing efforts in their work.

Applicants who prove to be competent for the post but who are not successful in this competition may be offered an appointment in another post of a similar nature, which might become vacant in the near future, albeit at the same or lower grade, provided they meet the necessary requirements.

We believe that all people are capable of great things. Because of this, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet all of the criteria listed within this job description.

HOW TO APPLY FOR A NATO CIVILIAN POST AT SHAPE:
Applications are to be submitted using NATO Talent Acquisition Platform (NTAP) (https://nato.taleo.net/careersection/2/jobsearch.ftl?lang-en). Applications submitted by other means (e.g. mail, e-mail, fax, etc) are not accepted.

postings.title: Office Head (Travel)
postings.description:
Post Context

Headquarters Allied Joint Force Command Norfolk (JFCNF) provides a resilient, static Joint headquarters to plan, prepare and conduct operations across all domains in peacetime, crisis and conflict, in order to support NATO’s three core tasks, at the Joint Operational level, as directed by SACEUR.

The Finance Directorate (J8) is responsible for all financial management operations and the correct application of all appropriated and non-appropriated funds approved for use by JFCNF.

The Finance and Accounting Branch is responsible for all financial and accounting activities related to international, multi-national credits, NATO Security Investment Programme (NSIP) projects and reimbursable activities.

The Travel Office is responsible for the provision of travel arrangements as well as the overall coordination of transportation services for personnel travelling on official duty provided either by Host Nation or by commercial sources.

Principal Duties:

- Responsible for all aspects of commercial Travel & Mobility for JFC HQ and supported elements.
- Plans, coordinates and supervises the execution of all duty travel in support of JFC HQ and supported elements activities including peacetime operations, exercises and deployments as well as out of region /area operations.
- Manages, plans and directs staff on the day to day management of the section.
- Liaises with the contracted Travel Agency ensuring that optimum service is provided in accordance with agreements.
- Makes decisions regarding the work priorities of the supporting staff to ensure that they match those of the head of the organization and the HQ.
- Plans the routing and itineraries of military and civilian personnel and determine locations, modes and facilities required for the movement of personnel and material by air, rail and surface means.
- Evaluates requests for Special Assignment Airlift missions and coordinates all travel requirements with military entities and commercial agencies to meet target dates.
- Processes all travel order applications, approves, authenticates as appropriate.
- Establishes the most suitable and cost effective mode of travel for each destination.
- Establishes reimbursable rates and, if required, provides information in support of the processing of claims for reimbursement of travel expenses submitted by the traveller.
- Establishes priorities and identifies the most effective method to utilize funds allocated for duty travel.
- Provides travel and cost related information to budget managers of functional areas if directed by Branch Head.
- Provides assistance and guidance to FinS Travel Module users; conducts on the job training and resolves FinS related issues.
- Maintains accurate financial and transactional records relating to HQ travel business.
- Certifies travel-invoices for payment.
- Ensures financial control measures are in place to prevent misuse or abuse.
- Monitors and reports on the performance of the Travel Contractor against the agreed contract. Proposes mitigating actions or process improvements as appropriate.
- Proactively participates in defining, mitigating and managing the risks within the functional area of responsibility in the Finance Directorate/J8 and actively contributes to implement and maintain the internal control framework of the Finance Directorate/J8.

Essential Qualifications / Experience:

- Higher Secondary education and completed higher vocational training leading to a formal technical or professional certification with 3 years function related experience, or Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 5 years post related experience.
- 4 years’ experience and knowledge in the field of commercial travel or transportation management.
- Experience in supervising and managing subordinated staff.
- Experience in office management, billing practices and associated record keeping.
- Experience involving contacts with commercial carriers and transport systems.

Language:

English - SLP 3322 - (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

Desirable Qualifications / Experience:

- Previous work experience in a NATO, military or International environment and work experience in the field of commercial travel and transportation management.
- Knowledge of the diplomatic, legal and customs regulations affecting travel to/through various countries.
- Familiar with USA & European railway, air and maritime booking systems.
- Experience in funds management, budgeting and accounting.
- Familiar with FinS and all its applications, in order to orchestrate the availability, access and use of the FinS travel module through the JFC HQ.
- FinS Travel Office and Travel FAO courses.

Attributes/Competencies:

Personal Attributes:

- Develops and implements innovative administrative policies and procedures directed at ensuring the highest level of organisational efficiency and productivity. Analyses problems, devises forms and methods to meet changing requirements.
- Acts as subject matter expert in formulating or revising directives and policies for JFC HQ and other NATO HQs. Uses own initiative to determine which course of action is necessary to resolve unexpected problems.
- Sound judgment and initiative are also required to establish priorities and identify the most effective method to utilise funds allocated for duty travel.
- Required to display creative thinking in proposing the adaptation of existing rules or creation of new procedures to comply with new situations such as crisis operations and out-of-area operations.
- Experience must enable the incumbent to undertake work in which considerable independence of thought and actions are required.
- Good health, stress tolerance and ability to work long hours when required. Must be capable of working in a demanding environment and have the necessary tact and personality to be able to work with staff, both military and civilian, at all levels and of different nationalities.

Managerial Responsibilities:

- Responsible for the planning of the day to day management of the section and directs the staff (one military workforce) accordingly.

Professional Contacts:

- The position involves professional contacts with managerial counterparts in NATO and outside immediate organisation with commercial carriers and various providers. Due to the nature of this post, the incumbent has frequent internal and external high-level contact including co-ordination and negotiation with senior civilians and military typically at OF4/ OF5 level, with whom discussions involve obligating resources of the organization and/ or formulation of policies take place.

Contribution To Objectives:

- Responsible for a crucial logistics support function, ensuring that operational requirements and target dates are met by coordinating transportation requirements with military and commercial agencies. The provision and procurement of travel services is not a purchasing activity, but a complex logistics support function, which falls directly under the responsibility of the incumbent.
- The incumbent's performance, guidance and knowledge have a significant financial impact on the JF HQ budget for travel. In addition to ensuring financial controls and protections are in place to avoid misuse or abuse, the incumbent is involved in many exceptional needs that arise. Ensuring that such needs, particularly those that have operational significance, are properly met, is an important part of the responsibilities of this post.
- The successful management of financial resources is considered vital to the achievement of the objectives and mission of the HQ. The incumbent contributes to mission objectives by establishing, monitoring and improving the travel process, in monitoring and simplifying internal procedures and in carrying out cost effective commitments. The incumbent's performance has a material impact on the travel budget and as such is critical to maintaining JF HQ and NATO's military capabilities.

Security Clearance

The successful applicant will be required to apply for and receive a NATO Secret Security Clearance prior to final confirmation of contract and commencement of employment.

The incumbent may be required to undertake deployments in support of military operations and exercises, and/or TDY assignments, both within and without NATO boundaries. Such operational deployment may exceed 30 days duration up to 183 days in any period of 547 days and may be on short notice. For NATO International Civilian staff, acceptance of an employment contract linked to this post constitutes agreement to deploy in excess of 30 days if required.

Contract

Serving NATO International Civilian staff will be offered a contract in accordance with the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations. Newly recruited staff will be offered a three year definite duration contract.

Notes for Candidates

The JFC Norfolk Website gives full details on the eligibility criteria and application processes to be adopted by all candidates. However, candidates should particularly note:

Please answer each of the pre-screening questions completely in English. Expressions such as: “please see attached CV, please see annex, please see enclosed document, etc” are not acceptable; this is a cause of immediate rejection of the application.

Particular attention should be given to Education and Experience section of your application form, which should be populated with details of your career to date and educational achievements and certifications as they relate to your application.

The candidature of NATO redundant staff at grade G10 will be considered with priority.

NATO reserves the right to screen applications to identify the use of such tools. All applications prepared, in whole or in part, by means of such generative or creative AI applications may be rejected without further consideration at NATO’s sole discretion, and NATO reserves the right to take further steps in such cases as appropriate.

postings.title: Principal Project Managers (Multiple Posts Available) - Brussels and The Hague
postings.description:
Who we are

For more than 75 years, NATO’s mission has been to preserve peace and security in the Alliance for nearly one billion citizens. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) and its predecessors have worked tirelessly in providing the means that enable the connectedness and togetherness that keep our Alliance strong. We are the NCIA, a team of 3400 civilian and military staff in 29 locations throughout Europe, North America and Asia.

Our technology and cyber experts allow NATO to conduct critical operations, protect NATO’s airspace, make data-driven decisions, defend against cyber-attacks, secure NATO networks and maintain superiority in space. This is all possible because of our greatest force, our people. In order to keep this edge we aim to hire, train and retain the very best talent.

Our staff members represent both the diversity and unity of our Alliance. When you join the NCIA, you will be part of an organisation where you can contribute authentically to the mission and purpose of NATO and help us keep our technological edge.

About the job

We are looking for experienced and motivated Principal Project Managers (G20) to join the organisation. Our G20 Principal Project Managers will be usually be based at either Brussels, Belgium or The Hague, Netherlands.

In this role, You will be a strategic leader planning the execution and delivery of complex, high-impact projects that support NATO’s digital transformation and strategic objectives. Working with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams, you will ensure that projects are delivered on time, within budget and to agreed quality standards in addition you will be responsible for:

· Project Leadership: Oversees the planning, implementation, and completion of complex projects, ensuring delivery on time, within scope and budget, and to defined quality standards.

· Stakeholder Management: Develops and executes comprehensive stakeholder strategies, builds long-term relationships with senior internal and external stakeholders, and acts as the primary point of contact for project-related matters.

· Governance & Assurance: Implements robust project monitoring, change control, risk management, and quality assurance processes. Ensures compliance with Agency procedures and manages project assurance activities.

· Business Risk & Change Management: Identifies, evaluates, and manages risks and change requests, ensuring effective mitigation and communication of impacts to stakeholders.

· Contract & Resource Management: Oversees contractual obligations, monitors performance using KPIs, and manages project resources, budgets, and reporting.

· Continuous Improvement: Drives operational excellence by capturing lessons learned, promoting best practices, and fostering a culture of continual improvement and innovation.

The Principal Project Manager demonstrates leadership in operational management, advises on opportunities for improvement, shares expertise to encourage team development, and proactively contributes to a culture of security, privacy, and ethics. By creatively applying innovative thinking and deputising for higher-grade staff as required, this role is pivotal in delivering value to NATO and its stakeholders, ensuring that projects not only meet their objectives but also support the broader mission of the NCIA.

This is a grouped campaign — a centralised recruitment process designed to identify and build a pool of qualified Principal Project Managers for deployment across multiple NCIA Organisational Elements . Successful candidates will be considered for current and future vacancies based on their experience, skill set and organisational fit.

At time of writing, there are a minimum of 7 x G20 Principal Project Manager posts that need to be filled from this campaign. It is possible that this number may go up or down throughout the lifetime of the hiring cycle.

For a full list of responsibilities, please review the job description here via the NCIA Career site

About you

You possess the ability to lead, inspire, and effectively engage a diverse and multidisciplinary team with tact, sound judgment, and adaptability. Additionally, your strong awareness, motivational skills, and attentive listening contribute to your capabilities, which include:

- A Master’s degree from a nationally recognised/certified university in a relevant discipline and at least five years of post-related experience; or a Bachelor’s degree with eight years of post-related experience.
- Demonstrated experience in project management of acquisition and/or development of complex projects within a large organisation.
- Strong proficiency in project management tools, cost control, and resource planning.
- Experience leading geographically dispersed teams, ideally within an international or multicultural environment.
- Proven expertise in stakeholder management and relationship building at senior levels.
- A recognised formal project management qualification such as PRINCE2 Practitioner or PMI-PMP.

Desirable:

- Previous experience within a defence, government, or multinational environment.
- Familiarity with NATO structures, governance, and processes.

You will also demonstrate:

- The ability to take initiative and make decisions independently.
- Strong organisational and communication skills.
- The capability to deliver results while fostering collaboration and continuous improvement.

What we offer

- Genuinely meaningful work supporting the most successful Alliance in history.
- A five-year contract with a competitive, tax-free monthly salary of 9,604.83 EUR (Belgium) or 10,628.93 EUR (Netherlands) and family allowances.
- Expatriation and education allowances (where applicable), plus additional home leave for expatriate staff.
- Excellent private health insurance scheme.
- 30 days of annual leave, plus official holidays.
- NATO Defined Contribution Pension Scheme.
- Development programmes including professional training, leadership courses, and wellbeing initiatives.

Additional Information

This recruitment is being conducted as part of a grouped campaign to fill multiple Principal Project Manager (G20) positions across several business areas. Candidates found qualified and suitable may be placed on a reserve list, which can be used to fill current vacancies, as well as anticipated requirements in 2027 and beyond.

The NCIA has other locations across Europe, and North America - and selected candidates may be considered for related opportunities depending on organisational needs.

This is an opportunity to join a large, strategic hiring campaign and contribute to critical NATO programmes that underpin the Alliance’s operational effectiveness.

If you are already a staff member within the NATO community seeking a new opportunity at the NCIA, it is strongly advised that you do not wait to see an advert from a particular Organisational Element, as recruitment for all G20 P3M talent will be derived from grouped campaigns.

To learn more about the NCIA and our work, please visit our careers site.

The NCIA prides itself on being an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment of mutual respect and value uniqueness and differences in gender, gender identity, race, ethnic or cultural origin, age, religion, sexual orientation and physical or neurocognitive ability.

Additional details on the conditions of application can be found via the NCIA career site.

Post Context

ACT contributes to preserving the peace, security and territorial integrity of Alliance member states by leading, at Strategic Command level, Warfare Development required to enhance NATO’s posture, military structures, forces, capabilities and doctrines.

The Capability Development Directorate (CAPDEV) comprises two Divisions—Requirements and Capabilities. The Directorate supports SACT in his Capabilities Requirement Authority (CRA) role. It is responsible for a holistic through lifecycle Capability Development approach that infuses innovation and transformative efforts that are an integral part of the Warfare Development. This includes responsibilities for elicitation, development, capture and collection, quality review, traceability and visibility of capability requirements.

The Capabilities Division coordinates the development of capabilities from capability planning through acceptance and then disposal with the management entities, NATO Headquarters staff and the NATO Governance Structure. This entails synchronizing horizontally across capabilities to achieve coherent efforts and outcomes.

The Communications Information Services (CIS) Branch leads the Core Services and Communication Services areas including IT Service Management and Deployable Communications Information System. Furthermore, the Branch leads the development of the NATO Enterprise Architecture for future C3 Information systems in accordance with approved NATO policy and links these architectures to the NDPP, the NSIP, and interoperability standards.

This post will act as a Programme manager for COI Enabling.

Principal Duties:

- Contribute to the development of Communications and Information Services (CIS):

- Ensure coherent elicitation of requirements as needed by the Requirements Division.

- Ensure accurate development of capability programme plans (CPPs) and ensure the delivery of programme outcomes by assessing throughout the life cycle the cost, scope, schedule, risk and performance.

- Ensure coordination and synchronization with all SMEs supporting warfare development at the management level, especially with the users and the host nations.

- Plan and lead acceptance with the support of relevant branches and in coordination with user and host nations.

- Provide programme and project expertise for ACT Programme of Work (POW) activities in CIS, Cyber, COI Enabling, Information Management and infrastructure and COI Services.

- In conjunction with the CIS Operating, Service Provisioning and Implementation Authorities, serve as a member of selected Integrated Coordination groups like the Capability Management Function and NATO HQ coordination groups (e.g. Integrated Project Steering Groups).

- Provides for Enterprise Architecture and capability architecture development.

- Brief the Military Committee, RPPB and IC as required on all technical aspects of CPP requirements and delivery.

- On transformational aspect:

- Support to the NATO Defence Planning Process (NDPP) Steps 2-5.

- Provide CIS service definition within the NATO structure; development of Mid-Term Plans (MTP); execution of NATO Defence Planning Processes (NDPP).

- Provide SME input and develop Capability Development Plans.

postings.title: Senior Analyst (Russia Cyber Domain/Red Team)
postings.description:
1. Post Context/Post Summary
Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) is the strategic level command responsible for the planning, preparation, conduct and execution of NATO operations, missions, activities and tasks as directed by Council in order to achieve the strategic objectives of the Alliance.
The Operations Directorate (OPS) is responsible for monitoring the strategic environment and manages current operations for the Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR). OPS directs and oversees all assigned operational and intelligence functional area activities through the J2 and the J3 divisions, coordinates the contribution of niche forces and capabilities (JTE, NUO, PRM, and ACCI), and tasks MOU organizations (NIFC, JEWCS).
The J2 Division provides comprehensive advice, warning, and situational awareness to the Command Group (CG) and Allied Command Operations (ACO) on Intelligence, Counter-Intelligence, Security, Information Security, Biometrics and Identity Intelligence, Geospatial, Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance (including ISTAR), Intelligence support to Joint Effects and Targeting, Intelligence Systems, Databases, and Interfaces, as well as Intelligence Support to other disciplines including red teaming.
The J2 Plans Branch is the focal point for all Intelligence related planning, policy and ETEE (Education, Training, Exercise and Evaluation) efforts, including a Red Team element that provides SACEUR and ACO with an independent analytical capability to challenge existing plans IOT enhance and improve SACEURs Decision Making Process (DMP). The Branch consists of two Sections: the Red Team and the J25 Intelligence Plans and Policy.

The Red Team is a multi-domain, multi-dimensional organizational element comprised of senior analysts that provides SACEUR and ACO with an independent analytical capability to challenge existing plans, operations and intelligence informed by Russian/Terrorist Groups Doctrine/TTPs in order to enhance the Decision Making Process (DMP) through structured and alternative analytical methods. The Red Team is to provide objective, independent strategic and predictive analysis and to contribute to a more comprehensive Common Intelligence Picture (CIP) in support of SACEURs DMP. This leads to greater situational understanding and in turn promotes greater situational awareness. The Section consists of two Teams: Red Cell and ETEE Cell.

2. Principal Duties
The incumbent is responsible for the independent, strategic, doctrinal and non-doctrinal analysis and the prediction of possible courses of actions (COAs), regarding the Russian Cyber domain and the identification and development of potential chances for the Alliance.
The incumbent’s duties are:
- As directed by the Red Team Section Head, analysing multi-domain and multidimensional, doctrinal and non-doctrinal, including TTPs and COAs, regarding Russian Cyber domain. Authoritative thinking and opinions from academia, think tanks and strategic studies institutes should be reflected.

Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) serves as NATO’s strategic command, responsible for planning, preparing and executing Alliance operations and activities. Within this Branch, the Situational Awareness Support Section analyses technical cyberspace vulnerabilities and drives consequence‑mitigating actions. The incumbent will support the integration and fusion of data feeds from multiple cyber tools, contribute to Fusion Analytics, and conduct data analysis in support of Defensive Cyberspace Operations and the integration of cyber effects in Multi‑Domain Operations.

1) Support for the production and review of the fusion products

2) Contribute and review the continuously updated threat picture, own system status and mission status input to cyber operational picture

3) Contribute to the activities related to integration and fusion of data feeds from different cyber tools( CDSA, CyCOP, CPAL, MISP, CySAS,Industry Feeds).

- Minimum 3 years of experience working in a military environment, with operational experience including experience in Operational Centres of higher formations.

- Knowledge and experience of cyber and cyber defence capabilities in relation to support of the operations of a large international, governmental or military organization

Description

The Joint Warfare Centre (JWC) is seeking an Industrial Security professional to join its Security Section within the Support Directorate. The position contributes to ensuring that classified information generated, shared, or managed under industrial contracts is safeguarded in accordance with NATO Security Policy and supporting directives.

Ø A meaningful role supporting NATO’s mission and readiness

Ø Work in a professional, international environment

Ø A key role in protecting classified information in industry contracts

Ø Exposure to NATO security policy and industrial security procedures

Ø Direct contribution to NATO training, exercises, and resilience

If you bring your expertise in industrial security, classified contracts management, and policy development, we encourage you to apply.

NATO Body: Joint Warfare Centre (JWC)

Ø To assist the JWC Security Office with general administrative tasks related to all security domains and support security operations related to exercises and events hosted at the JWC.

Ø Assists users in defining their access rights and privileges.

1. Post Context

Headquarters JSEC provides a resilient operational-level Joint Headquarters, capable of supporting 24/7 operations to coordinate enablement (at the operational level) and, on order, the execution of reinforcement by forces (RbyFo) and sustainment flow in order to contribute to the Alliance's ability to project and sustain combat power into, across and from the Area of Responsibility (AOR), and, if required, into a Joint Operations Area (JOA).

The Support Directorate (SPT) is responsible for providing cross-functional expertise in Supply and Services, HNS Military Engineering (MILENG), Medical Support, Maintenance, CIS, Human Resources (HR) matters and Logistics Information Management.

The J6 Division is responsible for developing and implementing policy, plans and procedures for CIS and Information Assurance (IA).

The Plans, Concepts and Information Assurance Branch is responsible for planning, development, execution, and enforcement of Command and Control (C2)-systems-related policy, concepts, IA and procedures in support of the HQ exercises and operations.

The incumbent contributes to CYBERSPACE / CIS operational planning and conduct of operations and exercises as an integral member of operational working groups. The incumbent plans and assesses CYBER / CIS requirements and capabilities for RbyFo and sustainment especially with contributions to doctrinal documents of JSEC.

2. Principal Duties

The incumbent's duties are:

Principle planning array J6 CYBERSPACE

-Establishes close relationship and works in close cooperation with SHAPE J6 / CyOC on strategic and all corresponding operational level entities within the functional domain JSEC.

-Plans and develops Concepts / Directives for the coordination of long-term CIS requirements for RbyFo and Sustainment.

-Contributes to Planning for future operations and exercises and support Deployment Planning.

-Coordinates with NATO Communications & Information Systems Group (NCISG), NATO Communications & Information Agency (NCIA) and host, sending, receiving nation for long-term CIS requirements for operations and exercises.

-Supports and assesses all CIS Interoperability related policy, concepts, and procedures with special focus on NATO digital transformation 2030.

-Is in divisional lead for preparation, contribution, coordination and the developing of measures to NATO Crises Response System (NCRS) throughout JSECs functional area.

For NATO International Civilian Staff, acceptance of an employment contract linked to this post constitutes agreement to deploy in excess of 30 days if required.

a. Professional Experience

Activities that ensure consideration of Communications and Information System (CIS) and Cyber Defence aspects during the production of an Operational Plan. CIS must be deployed, maintained, protected and defended to achieve maximum overall effectiveness in the employment of military forces consistent with the projected rate of activity and scope of operations. Cyberspace planners should be brought into the planning process at the beginning and must interact continuously with those who will conduct operations.

- This role requires proven experience in Command and Control Support (Operational Planning - Spectrum Management).

Activities that coordinate the NATO Military use of the Electromagnetic Spectrum at strategic, operational, and tactical levels by national, international, military and governmental agencies and staffs. This includes the production and co-ordination of the EMCON plan and its operation. Comprehensive management of the spectrum, used for all military purposes (not just CIS), by qualified persons, in order to ensure the most effective use of the limited bandwidths and frequencies within a joint force and between adjacent and higher authorities.

b. Education/Training

University Degree and 2 years function related experience, or Higher Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 4 years post related experience.

The additional job specific qualifications and experience are described under Professional Experience paragraph. In case of ambiguity the required job specific experience has priority over the standard education and training levels and experience described here.

English - SLP 3333 - (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

Education/Training

Any further training certificates and courses related to subject field or acquired through NATO (e.g.: Spectrum Management for NATO, NATO Comprehensive Operations Planning Course, NATO C4ISR Orientation for Officers, NATO CIS Operational Planning, NATO Deployed Spectrum Management for Operations and Exercises).

6. Attributes/Competencies

a. Personal Attributes

The duties require clarity of thought, sound consistent judgement, good interpersonal and communication skills and often a creative approach to bridge the challenge of the diverse application of varying standards on CIS/Cyber. The incumbent must possess creativity and originality, and ability to deal with projects with confidentiality. Must be a mature articulate individual possessing tact and sound judgment. Principal Duties:

The incumbent's duties are:

- Manages directly the daily operations related to the HQ SACT finance and accounting team.

- Primary Deputy to the ACT Section Head (Treasury and Accounting)/ACT Chief Accountant).

- Is the primary contributor to the ACT Chief Accountant on developing ACT-wide financial management policy, contributing specific expertise in the areas of reimbursable activities, infrastructure transactions and travel.

- Deputizes for the ACT Chief Accountant in the NATO Accounting Working Group to ensure that ACT accounting issues are represented in the development of NATO Strategic level accounting policy.

- Is the principal contributor to the technical accounting work required to support the ACT Chief Accountant in the production of the ACT Consolidated Financial Statements.

postings.title: Visiting Researcher Programme (VRP)
postings.organisation: Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE)
postings.description:
**Applications are currently being accepted and will be considered on a monthly basis for existing project requirements**

1. POST CONTEXT

The Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE) is an organization of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), an established world-class scientific research and experimentation facility that organizes and conducts scientific research and technology development, centred on the maritime domain, delivering innovative and field tested Science & Technology (S&T) solutions to address defence and security needs of the Alliance.

The CMRE Visiting Researcher Programme is designed to support the Research Division (RD) and the Engineering and Information Technology Division (EITD) in developing their programme of work. The Programme offers the best and brightest students and university researchers from NATO nations the opportunity to participate in a dynamic, scientific team, conducting research on subjects of interest to both the researcher and to NATO. Researchers will have access to CMRE equipment, facilities, and data, and will gain practical experience through collaboration with CMRE scientists and engineers.

Applications are currently being accepted and will be periodically considered for existing project requirements.

Successful candidates will contribute to CMRE's core competencies and current projects. CMRE's core competencies include:

- Underwater acoustics
- Underwater Robotics
- Seismic acoustic
- Sensors and signal processing
- Ocean observation and prediction
- Operations research of complex systems
- Remote sensing and adaptive sampling
- Underwater communication engineering
- Ocean and marine engineering
- Unmanned underwater and aerial vehicles (sensors, payloads, platforms)
- Information theory
- Cognitive science
- Autonomy and collective intelligence
- AI
- Climate change and Security
- Compact fuel cell power modules (robots and drones)
- Virtual reality
- Data exploitation
- Quantum Technology
- Computer Science
- Cybersecurity
- System Administration
- Cloud computing
- Networking
- Modelling and Simulation
- IT support/Helpdesk

Current research programmes based on these competencies include autonomous mine countermeasures, cooperative anti-submarine warfare, data and environmental knowledge and operational effectiveness, and maritime security. Applicants are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the technical content of the Centre's current research efforts, and tailor their applications accordingly.

2. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

To apply for the Visiting Researcher Programme you must fulfil below criteria on the date of your application:

- University Degree (Bachelor's or Master's Degree) in a related field.
- English SLP 3333.

Notes to Applicants

- Research Fellows fall within the category of Consultants and chapter XVI of NATO CPRs regulates them.
- Research Fellows' assignments will last a minimum of 90 consecutive days and may be extended by one further period not exceeding 90 days. On a case-by-case basis, assignments shorter than 3 months may be accepted.
- Research Fellows will receive paid travel to and from their place of residence to the CMRE in accordance with NATO travel rules, unless the assignment is less than 30 consecutive calendar days.
- Research Fellows are reminded that it is their responsibility to investigate with their appropriate Authorities in their home country whether a VISA is required for them to work in Italy and for their family members to join them in Italy. The related costs will not be covered by CMRE.
- Research Fellows salaries are not exempted from taxation, therefore, they are responsible to declare their salaries received from CMRE to the appropriate Fiscal Authorities, as required by legislation.
- Research Fellows are not automatically insured for accidents (to include accidents on duty), health problems or other risks, therefore, insurance coverage is mandatory. They need to provide evidence of insurance coverage for illness, accidents and accidents on duty for the whole period at CMRE.
- Research Fellows will be required to sign a statement understanding that all proprietary rights in any work carried out under the VRP shall be vested in the organisation. They will also be required to participate in a security briefing upon arrival.
- Research Fellows' Salary: 3,079.45 (EUR) Monthly.
- If you are an undergraduate, you can apply to the Visiting Researcher Programme as a Research Intern, with the corresponding salary of 1,375.46 (EUR) Monthly.

Application procedure

- Applicants should submit their applications through NATO Talent Acquisition Program (NTAP) and they may propose their own topic of research for consideration when aligning candidate interests with CMRE project requirements.
- Application is limited to nationals of NATO member states: Albania, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, The Netherlands, Türkiye, United Kingdom and United States.
- Candidates must be at least 21 years old to be considered for the Visiting Researcher Programme. On a case-by-case basis, participation to the VRP may require the researcher to obtain a NATO Secret security clearance certificate or interim clearance issued by the national authorities of the researcher's country of origin prior to arrival.

Our recruitment process

- Please note that we can only accept applications from nationals of NATO member countries.
- Applications for this vacancy (including the most relevant publications, the diplomas - stating the highest level of education - and a CV) must be submitted using the E-recruitment system – NTAP.
- When submitting your application, please note that you are applying for a candidate pool, and not for a particular assignment. You will receive an acknowledgement of receipt of your application from the system. This being an open call for applications, you should not expect to receive any feedback on your candidature, unless selected for an interview for a specific assignment.

- The selection process will be based on CV screening and remote interview with the subject matter expert. The final decision on the appointment of the selected Research Fellow will stay with CMRE Director.

Additional information

- CMRE values diverse backgrounds and perspectives and is committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and talented workforce. We welcome applications of nationals from all Member States and strongly encourage women to apply.

- Selected candidates are expected to be role models of integrity, and to promote good governance through ongoing efforts in their work.

- Research fellows will be invited to a dedicated community of STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) professionals in the Science and Technology Organization (STO), whose main goal is to inform STO’s efforts and widen the NATO scientific knowledge base, with personal and community growth as main objectives.

NOTE:

NATO will not accept any phase of the recruitment and selection process, in whole or in part, by means of generative artificial-intelligence (AI) tools, including and without limitation to chatbots, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (Chat GPT), or other language generating tools. NATO reserves the right to screen applications to identify the use of such tools. All applications prepared, in whole or in part, by means of such generative or creative AI applications may be rejected without further consideration at NATO’s sole discretion, and NATO reserves the right to take further steps in such cases as appropriate.

For more information on how to apply:
